name: John Charles Tashner Jr.

roles.title: Radioman, Commander Patrol Wing TWO, Pearl Harbor
Radioman second class, USS Ballard, at Midway
In charge of a maintenance crew detachment, Betio, Tarawa Atoll
Chief radioman, electronics division, fleet plane pool at Majuro

summary: Jay Tashner's Navy career ran from a peacetime deck force to the age of airborne radar, and passed through nearly every hinge of the Pacific war on the way. Born in Jersey City on 18 December 1920 and raised in Lynchburg, Virginia, he enlisted at seventeen in October 1938, served two years in the destroyer USS Selfridge (DD-357), and transferred into naval aviation at Pearl Harbor in July 1941. On the morning of 7 December he was a twenty-year-old radioman of Patrol Wing TWO, ashore in a barracks — handed a rifle in the confusion, then set to days of recovering the dead from the oil-covered harbour, a morning he spoke of afterwards almost not at all. Six months later, aboard the seaplane tender USS Ballard, he stood radio watches through the Battle of Midway and shared in the capture of the survivors of the sunken carrier Hiryū, taken from an open boat two weeks after the battle — thirty-six officers and men by his record's count. He became an in-flight radio instructor and combat aircrewman at San Diego, made the invasion landing on Tarawa with CASU-16 and ran an aircraft-maintenance detachment on Betio, then headed the electronics division of the fleet plane pool at Majuro as a chief radioman, twice commended in 1944. He refused a wartime commission — his sons remember his reasons differently — married Margaret Monroe Holston, and after the war followed his trade into the electronic age until he was flying TBM-3W radar aircraft with anti-submarine squadron VS-22 as an airborne early warning and ASW operator-technician. He retired in 1958 as a chief petty officer with four children to raise, and died in September 1977.

sources.note: the whole shape of the career: Norfolk from October 1938, Selfridge April 1939 – July 1941, VP-23 and Patrol Wing TWO at Pearl Harbor, Ballard at Midway and the thirty-six captured, the combat aircrewman designation, the Tarawa landing and Betio, Majuro and the 1944 commendations, and the postwar run to AEW/ASW.
